mainTopic: How בית שמאי and בית הלל read a conditional נזירות vow about a lying cow, and how the case is adjusted to fit רבי יהודה and בית הלל's own rulings
overview: The גמרא is explaining the case behind the משנה's dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל. A cow is lying down. A man vows to be a נזיר on the condition that the cow does not stand, and then it gets up by itself. בית שמאי say he meant 'if I do not stand it up,' so the vow takes effect. בית הלל say he meant 'if it does not end up standing,' so the vow does not take effect. The גמרא challenges this from רבי יהודה's wording about a קרבן, because in a vow from wine nothing about the cow becomes forbidden. So it changes the case to a vow of נזירות from the cow's own meat. That raises a new question: בית הלל hold that נזירות from meat never takes effect, so why would the cow's standing matter to them? The answer is that בית הלל were arguing on בית שמאי's terms: even if such a vow works, the cow stood, so it should fail. בית שמאי reply that the man's point was standing it up himself, which he never did.

steps.title: The cow case: a vow of נזירות from wine if the cow does not stand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets the משנה in a case where a man vowed to be a נזיר from wine if a lying cow does not stand, and the cow got up by itself. בית שמאי say the vow takes effect. בית הלל say it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: 'I am a נזיר from wine if it does not stand up,' and it stood up on its own. בית שמאי think: this man's real point was that he himself would make it stand, and he did not, so the vow takes effect. בית הלל think: his point was only that it was lying down, and now it is standing, so the vow does not take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its picture of the case behind the משנה: a vow tied to whether a lying cow will stand. It then gives each side's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole argument is about what the man really meant. בית שמאי read his words as 'if I don't make it stand,' and since he did not stand it up himself, the condition was met and he is a נזיר. בית הלל read them as 'if it doesn't stand,' and since it did stand, the condition was not met and he is not a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: I am hereby a נזיר (the standard wording for taking on נזירות)
by itself, on its own
literally his weak spot; here, the core of what he meant
making it stand with his own hand
lying down

steps.confusionAlert: Be careful with the direction of the condition. 'If it does NOT stand' means the vow takes effect only if the cow fails to stand (by his reading, if he fails to stand it up). So בית שמאי, who say he never stood it up himself, are the ones who say he IS a נזיר.

phrases.english: and he said: "I am hereby a nazirite from wine
if it does not stand,"
phrases.notes: 'It' is a cow lying down in front of him.

phrases.english: and it stood up on its own.
Beit Shammai hold:
this man's real intention
is about making it stand with his own hand,
and he did not make it stand.
And Beit Hillel hold:
it is about the fact that it was lying down,
and it has stood up.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי סָבְרִי: תּוּרְפֵּיהּ דְּהַאי גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the גמרא's explanation of the case in the משנה, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: the vow takes effect because he did not stand the cow up himself. בית הלל: no vow, because the cow stood.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's wording about a קרבן does not fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the explanation. רבי יהודה says בית שמאי meant only someone who said 'they are a קרבן upon me,' but in this case nothing is being made into a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the last part of the משנה: רבי יהודה said that even בית שמאי only meant a person who said 'they are a קרבן upon me.' But in this case, does he attach anything to the cow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation from step 1 using the last clause of the משנה, רבי יהודה's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's words assume the man made some object forbidden by calling it a קרבן. In the case from step 1, the cow is only a condition, and the vow is about wine. So nothing is forbidden as a קרבן, and רבי יהודה's clause makes no sense in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
say the last clause (of the משנה)
an offering; here, a vow that makes an item forbidden like an offering
attaches or links a prohibition to an item

phrases.english: If so, say the last clause:
Rabbi Yehuda said:
even when Beit Shammai said it,
they said it only about one who says
"They are hereby an offering upon me."

phrases.aramaic: פָּרָה מִי קָא מַתְפֵּיס בָּהּ מִידֵּי?
phrases.english: Does he attach anything to the cow?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case explanation from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the vow was 'nazir from wine' with the cow only as a condition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה speaks of something becoming a קרבן, which requires the vow to forbid an actual object. In this case no object is forbidden.

steps.title: Reworded case: a vow of נזירות from the cow's meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the case: the man said 'I am a נזיר from its meat if it does not stand.' Now the cow itself is involved in the vow. בית שמאי and בית הלל keep the same reasoning as before.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a case where he said: 'I am a נזיר from its meat if it does not stand,' and it stood up on its own. בית שמאי think his point was standing it up himself, and he did not. בית הלל think his point was that it was lying down, and now it is standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing the man's words, so that the vow is about the cow's own meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the vow now forbids the cow's meat, an actual object is involved, which fits רבי יהודה's talk of a קרבן. The reasoning of the two sides stays exactly the same; only the subject of the vow changes from wine to the cow's meat.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (bringing a new explanation)
for example; a case where
from its meat

phrases.english: Rather, it is a case where he said
"I am hereby a nazirite from its meat
if it does not stand," and it stood up on its own.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי סָבְרִי: תּוּרְפֵּיהּ דְּהָהוּא גַּבְרָא
phrases.english: Beit Shammai hold: that man's real intention
is about making it stand with his own hand,
and he did not make it stand.
And Beit Hillel hold:
this man's real intention is about the fact that it was lying down,
and it has stood up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2 by replacing the case from step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case (changes the wording of the vow)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow was 'nazir from wine,' with the cow only as a condition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow was 'nazir from its meat,' so the cow's meat is the object of the vow, which fits רבי יהודה's wording.

steps.title: But according to בית הלל, a vow of נזירות from meat is not נזירות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new case from בית הלל's side. Their reasoning suggests that if the cow had not stood, he would be a נזיר. But בית הלל hold that saying 'a נזיר from meat' makes no one a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do בית הלל really hold that if the cow did not stand, he would be a נזיר? But they said that someone who says 'from its meat' is not a נזיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge against the reworded case from step 3, this time from בית הלל's own ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל's reasoning makes the whole thing depend on whether the cow stands. That suggests the vow would take effect if it did not stand. But בית הלל hold that נזירות 'from meat' is meaningless and never takes effect, just like their ruling on dried figs in the משנה. So the condition should not matter at all.

keyTerms.meaning: he is (becomes) a נזיר
but didn't they say? (a challenge from someone's own ruling)

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge is aimed at בית הלל, not בית שמאי. The point is that בית הלל's reasoning about the cow standing would be unnecessary if the vow could never take effect anyway.

phrases.english: And do Beit Hillel hold
that if it did not stand, he would be a nazirite?
But didn't they say that if he says "from its meat" he is not a nazirite!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל סָבְרִי אִי לָא קָמַת הָוֵי נָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reworded case from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'nazir from its meat' case as it applies to בית הלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בית הלל's reasoning implies the vow would work if the cow did not stand. But they hold that נזירות from meat never takes effect, so whether the cow stands should be irrelevant.

steps.title: בית הלל were arguing on בית שמאי's terms
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל do not really think he would be a נזיר. They are telling בית שמאי: even by your view, the vow should not take effect, because the cow stood up.
steps.simpleTranslation: They spoke according to בית שמאי's reasoning. In our view, even if the cow did not stand, he would not be a נזיר. But you say he is a נזיר. So at least admit to us that this man's condition was about the cow lying down, and it did stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 4. בית הלל were not giving their own view. They were arguing with בית שמאי using בית שמאי's own assumptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that בית הלל seemed to say he would be a נזיר if the cow had not stood. The answer is that בית הלל hold he is never a נזיר from meat. Their point is only this: even if we grant בית שמאי that such a vow works, the man's condition was about the cow lying down, and it stood up, so the vow should not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: According to their reasoning, arguing on the other side's terms
According to us, in our own view
At least admit to us
The main point or heart of the matter, what his condition really depends on
Lying down

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think בית הלל changed their opinion. They still hold that 'a נזיר from meat' makes no one a נזיר. Here they are only arguing 'even according to you.'

phrases.english: They spoke according to the reasoning of בית שמאי:
According to us, even if it did not stand,
he would also not be a נזיר.
According to you, who say he is a נזיר,
at least admit to us
that the main point of this man's condition
is about the fact that it was lying down,
and look, it did stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 4 against בית הלל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Argument on the other side's terms (לטעמייהו)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית הלל seemed to hold that he would be a נזיר if the cow had not stood, which goes against their own view on 'a נזיר from meat.'
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל hold he is never a נזיר here. They only argue that even by בית שמאי's view, the condition about the lying cow was not met, since it stood.

steps.title: בית שמאי's reply: the condition was about his own action
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי explain that the man meant 'if I do not make it stand.' He did not make it stand, so the vow takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית שמאי say: wasn't this man's main point that he would make the cow stand with his own hand? And he did not make it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives בית שמאי's side. It explains why they still say the vow takes effect, even though the cow stood up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides read the man's condition differently. בית הלל say it was about the cow's position, and the cow stood. בית שמאי say it was about whether he himself got the cow up. Since the cow got up by itself and he never stood it up, the case he described ('if I do not make it stand') actually happened, so the vow takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Making it stand with his own hand
Isn't it? Used here to start a rhetorical question

steps.whatToRemember: The argument is about what the man really meant. בית הלל: 'if the cow does not end up standing.' בית שמאי: 'if I do not get it to stand.' The cow got up by itself, so the vow fails by בית הלל's reading and works by בית שמאי's reading.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a נזיר vow with a condition depends on what the person really meant by the condition, not only on what happened.

phrases.english: And בית שמאי:
Isn't the main point of this man's condition
about making it stand with his own hand?
And look, he did not make it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי: לָאו תּוּרְפֵּיהּ דְּהַאי גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives בית שמאי's reply to the reasoning בית הלל offered in Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reading of the man's condition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the cow stood, it might seem that בית שמאי should also agree that his condition ('if it does not stand') was not met, so the vow does not take effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי read the condition as being about the man raising the cow himself. He did not, so the vow takes effect.
